rules.message: P2 — `unity open` with no path does NOT resolve the cwd. It launches a second, bare Editor on the project picker and reports no error. Pass an explicit path.
P2 — `unity editors running` has misreported which instance has the project open, listing both PIDs. Cross-check process command lines.
P2 — `unity pipeline list` resolves the CURRENT DIRECTORY as the project and invents a row when there isn't one. `cd` to the project first, use `--json`, and read `pipelineServer.isReachable`.
P1 — The Editor snapshots its cloud access token AT STARTUP. `unity auth login` must run BEFORE launching the Editor.
P1 — Unity does not resolve a `Packages/manifest.json` change made while it is running. The Editor must be restarted.
P1 — `uv` must be on the Editor's PATH at launch. Installing it while Unity runs leaves MCP reporting 'uv not found in PATH'.
P3 — `unity mcp configure` does its work and then NEVER EXITS. Give it a timeout and verify side-effects rather than waiting on exit.
P3 — UnityYAMLMerge blocks on a GUI on unparseable input. Pass `-h --fallback none` for non-interactive use.

P1 — Check `unity status --json` before the first Editor-bound MCP call. Every Unity MCP server in this manifest advertises its full tool catalogue whether or not an Editor is running, so the presence of these tools is NOT evidence one exists. With `count: 0` the call blocks the full timeout (60s on the official arm, ~20s on coplay) and returns a timeout or `no_unity_session` without ever naming the missing precondition. The check costs ~200ms; the failure costs up to a minute per call. If no Editor is running, use the `unity` CLI instead.

P2 — `get_scene_hierarchy` takes only `path` — no depth or limit. Unscoped on a real scene it returned 290,642 characters across 7,883 lines, overflowing the tool-result budget and spilling to a file. Pass `path` to scope it to the subtree you actually need.
P5 — CoplayDev writes do not echo state. Read the state back explicitly after any mutation.

P4 — Most Unity MCP arms are TWO pieces: a server process and an Editor-side package. Installing one gives you a server connected to nothing, which answers liveness checks while every real call fails. anklebreaker needs unity-mcp-plugin alongside the Node server; realvirtual needs the Python server downloaded from its Editor toolbar; codergamester's Node bridge does nothing until the Unity package has built it. Run `mcp-cocktail install <arm>` and complete every step, not just the shell one.
